reviews.text: 发售半年后的秋促改好评，经过几次更新，大部分首发的恶性bug已经基本都修复了，好玩爱玩 ------------------------------------------------ 我以为的这次的重置版是类似暗黑破坏神3一样把fate的4部游戏变成4个可以传送的地图，结果是开始游戏前需要先手动选择玩第几部？？？这样还算是一个完整的游戏吗？？？四个存档不互通，人物、任务的进度相当于独立，最多也就只能做到在第4部导入前3部的角色，那我为什么不去专注于玩原版的某一部呢？？？单单这一条游戏性方面的缺点就已经够致命了，而且中文的本地化也做得很差，例如高达159RMB的售价，一股老外口音的中文语音，连最基本的文字排版都没有做好，界面上的很多文字是重叠在一起的。实在看不出来这作重置版的诚意

This series was my childhood, I'm so glad to see it updated for modern systems. If you need any convincing, the first cast of my fishing rod into the river in Grove and I caught Peronto's Cheesehead of the Emerald Bay, so I feel like that's a good sign.

Great remaster, and comes with QOL changes such as items introduced in sequels now being in every game even when they weren't there originally. You can also select your race in every game now, and the Demon race introduced in Cursed King is now available in all 4 games. The music is the exact same as the originals and the graphics look a lot better than the demo. A must buy if you're a fan of the classic Fate games.

I was really looking forward to this but it feels like it released to early. I do like some of the QOL things that were added but the bugs and visuals really need to be addressed. Some textures and models feel like they have been updated and given a refresh while others still look low poly and low res which causes severe clashing with the art style. There are also a handful of bugs that, while not game breaking, are just annoying to deal with. Also this might just be a minor nitpick but the quest rewards and boss drops do not feel balanced, I got boots that required over 100 strength to wear from a boss drop on level 1. If they go back and fix the bugs and sort out the situation going on with the textures I'll revise my review to a positive one, It just doesn't feel that great to play compared to the original games atm.

Fair warning the mechanics of having your inventory screens available while moving is gone. Not only that but the item stat screen is shoved into the bottom right hand corner and it really ruins the fluidity of how the first games played. Honesty kinda upsetting considering how much i love the Fate series but come on. The way the game was played and the way it "felt" is not he same. Going in and out of menus and having to look on the other side of the screen for item stats is super annoying. If you didnt play the first games you might not bat an eye at it but it feels way more clunky and not very fluid. Ill change my review to positive if they give us UI options. I feel like having either a customizable UI or even just a legacy option would be great and would make a lot of players very happy. i enjoy the new hotbar but also some players dont because its way smaller which is totally understandable. Its primarily the UI and how it feels but tbh thats what made fate so appealing to me in the first place and now its gone.

I'm seeing a lot of derision from the long time fans, which is genuinely a shame. As somebody spurned by bad remasters before, I hate to see long time supporters upset. However, as somebody who played the demo as a kid, I'm more than happy. I bought the original releases last year, but didn't like how they looked on my computer (stretched and odd). I could have fixed that, sure, but I heard a remaster was on the way, so I waited patiently. Now that Remaster is out, I can say with confidence that it is everything I wanted and more. A comfy little Diablo like, no frills, just cozy and fun. This is worth the price of admission if you want a game like that, a good dungeon crawler with loot, that isn't too difficult and is pretty adorable to look at.

So this could be quite a fun remake of the old games but at this point you are better off playing the originals than playing this even with the issues that they have. There are a number of issues I have spotted within the first 1.5 hours of playtime 1. You cannot get to your pet inventory without opening yours up first and then clicking on the pet Icon. This could be solved by allowing you to click p and it directly opens the pet inventory. 2. On the topic of inventory click and hold to move items is painful. Make it so you click to pick up an item and click to drop or give an option to switch between the modes. 3. You cannot shift click items into the anvil (I assume the enchanter as well). This combined with issue 2 makes enchanting very annoying. [strike]4. Knockback on the spell ringing blast knocks enemies back and sometimes forward and sometimes not at all but the enemy stands there distracted doing nothing for a couple seconds.[/strike] Fixed as of patch 1.02 5. On the topic of spells you need to close the inventory to cast identify. This is absurdly stupid. I do not want to have to close my inventory to cast a spell to identify one item then exit the menu for the next one. (This alone makes me think the devs have never properly played an ARPG) 6. You cannot swap spells until after you have completely finished casting the prior one. This is annoying as hell when casting multiple buffs. In the old games you could swap as soon as you hit the cast button. Fix this and swapping spells will be way less annoying. I don't know how many times I have healed myself and hit the button for my attack spell and then I heal myself at the start of the next combat because I didn't notice it hadn't swapped. 7. I attack a barrel and a random one out of my range behind me gets destroyed. 8. Enemies get screwed up when you have summons. They keep trying to jump between different summons and start running around like fools. 9. The targeting size of enemies is way too darn big. I try to click to the side of them to get close to cast a spell and I end up attacking with my very slow weapon attack speed and take some hits. (hasn't killed my hardcore character yet but has dropped my hp drastically) 10. When using keyboard and mouse have the popup showing you are selecting to use the portal/fish/descend deeper appear above the thing instead of the top middle of the screen. I am looking at the middle of my screen or where my mouse is not the top of the screen. I have already tried to click on a portal multiple times and due to not reading I descend a flood instead of heading back to town. 11. The lava type floor seems to cause alot of lag when running with haste. I have a decent pc so this is an optimization issue. It has happened in other areas but this was the most noticeable and repeatable Onto my more petty complaints that may just be personal preference 12. For the original Fate move the portal back by the fountain in the center. It was much more convenient to be closer to the center near more vendors and the healer. 13. Why did you not give an identify scroll at the start like the original games do? It is a slight annoyance but for someone who has started alot of runs over the years I can tell you that this will get annoying. 14. I really don't like the location of the stamina bar. This is purely personal preference but I like having the bar more in the center where I will notice it more easily and not run out of stamina without noticing. 15. Attack animations are missing the feeling of any sort of actual impact. I don't know what it is exactly but after playing the old game to this the animations are all just a bit soft for lack of a better word. 16. The magical sword creature looks pathetic. It used to be a massive floating purple saber and now it is this tiny arse thing that is hard to see with some particle effects around it. 17. When using the stop fishing button it should not do the same animation of trying to catch. The old games would just bring in the rod without the animation of looking at your fishing line if you hit stop fishing. With the way it is now the stop fishing button is useless. As for the positives for the game that I have noticed. 1. They made quest rewards actually rewarding and worth doing so there is that. 2. They have updated it so I have hopes that they will fix the issues and make this game a worthy successor

I like the new fresh style. However I've found a few things the old versions had that this new version doesn't. First I miss the buttons on the hotbar for inventory, quest, and spellbook. I miss playing one handed and in comfortable positions. Second holding the shift key and clicking merchants to let my pet sell items instead of having to sell items from my inventory, exit, open my pet's inventory, and then talk to the merchant again. Also stamina seems to run out a lot faster then the older versions. Third when moving things in your inventory you can't move things one top of each other for quick and easy organization like in the older versions. The big positives I have to can see in this version is there are way more options for character customization and pet choices. I love the new styles and reskins for some of the armor and weapons as well. There's still a lot more I have to see in this which I'm excited to find but this is my initial observations. I hope some of the above mentioned things get implemented eventually.

This is a low effort remastering of a classic game that deserved more care and more time to bake in the oven. The updated visuals here are the best part but a lot of the other aspects just feel off. It's a bit hard to describe and see until you actually play the game yourself. Here are some but not all of the issues present : AI and player plathing took a huge hit. Obstacle avoidance is really bad compared to the original games. Breakable objects are no longer highlighted. Swing animations are no longer varied and are missing early breakouts for new fast attacks. Attack ranges are off. The player overall runs way slower. Most of the ambient noises from the originals are missing. The amount of hotbar slots you get were reduced, you can't shift click to have your pet pick up things anymore and the list goes on and on and on. Inventory management just simply sucks here. Usually when a game gets remastered new QoL is added into the game -- not taken away. That is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lame. There was a great opportunity here to add in local splitscreen co-op, online multiplayer, or ANY KIND of multiplayer functionality that would actually make this game have any lasting power. There was such a good opportunity here to have FATE last another decade but as it is this game will just fade into obscurity again because they took the low effort approach. Save yourself your $25. If you're a big FATE fan then maybe wait until this goes on sale for $10. Or even better yet buy the original games. They are much better than this utter garbage dollar store ass rehashing.

I think most people looking at this game are coming from the perspective of having played the OG FATE games long ago, in a land forgotten by time known as "WildTangent." Coming from this perspective, FATE: Reawakened has proven to be rather polarizing for two primary reasons: 1.) More bugs than a garbage truck upon release. 2.) UI is a [i]heavy[/i] departure from the source material. Regarding the bugs, they have been steadily killed off by a number of post-release patches which are still ongoing. The developer is engaged with the community and actively working on debugging, which is nice. The UI is hard to argue against; the originals have a certain "budget 2006 PC Diablo-clone" appeal which is not replicated by the remaster. In optimizing for console / controller, the UI comes across as samey and bland. I really hate sounding like a pretentious mong with the whole "the objectively worse-looking and janky version is better," but that is an aspect of FATE that I do quite miss. I think I've complained enough so here are some positives: 1.) All 4 games in one convenient package. 2.) QoL changes, spells, characters, pets, and equipment from later games are retroactively added to earlier installments. 3.) You can import characters between games if you choose, but only sequentially from 1>2>3>4. Overall I thi [b]You are overburdened Your review is full You cannot type any more[/b]

Fate Reawakened +Playable with gamepad(not sure if the originals were) +Playable at '4k' +Performance is good at a locked 120 FPS(for my system, specs at the bottom) -Too many missing QoL features -No identify/portal book stacking or auto-storing scrolls -Crashed four times so far -Ranged(and sometimes briefly others) enemies constantly running out of melee range -Fishing often takes way too long(sometimes even around a minute) -Placing/positioning items in inventory needs a lot of precision resulting in many failed attempts(no 'snapping' function) -Replacing items(the position) in inventory doesn't work at all -Game generally didn't age well, especially without heavy QoL work -Pet/minion pathfinding is really bad with them regularly getting stuck and not doing anything -No game mechanics are explained anywhere it seems(not even race bonuses at character creation) -No list of all active stat bonuses -Levels are all incredibly basic/empty and use rectangular/square layouts every time -No possibility to view entire level map, only parts of it at a time -Starting from The Traitor Soul, the new enemies have absolutely broken/missing animations -Starting from The Traitor Soul, I noticed a LOT of missing/broken sounds even after restarts -I've had my pet's entire inventory wiped several times now(not because of selling, but from entering portals it seems) -New textures seem AI-generated/upscaled -'Body type' in character creation - this needs to stop Played as melee character first which was frustrating as enemies often run away(and getting 'knockback' stat on a piece of gear makes it even worse, requiring constant repositioning). After 'finishing' the game that way, I played as a summoner but that was even more frustrating, due to summoned minions getting stuck constantly(as mentioned above). All in all no, I don't recommend this(maybe at 75% or higher off in it's current state for pure nostalgia) - it still needs some heavy QoL work. Too much is missing/broken. Specs for any interested: 4080 SUPER i9-10900K 64GB RAM Windows 10 64-bit

Honestly my childhood nostalgia brought back. And while I absolutely love this game and it's dear to me with there also being very limited to almost no game exactly like this it has many faults that hold this back a lot from being so SO much more. From seemingly poor choices in RA that are downgrades from the original. [Examples]: - Can't have inventory open while fishing - Less potion slots - Debuff timer not on the hud but in inventory screen And trust me more in! The list I share ranges from straight up why the hell were some of these features not added ESPECIALLY with this being a modernization of the classic and this being 2026 to just pet peeves or QOL that is drastically needed. There is a lot of what are basic staple features that would only add to this experience with ZERO con to it. Regardless of it trying to keep the nostalgia alive, they made a remaster/update to the games. The "argument" no longer applies when the goal was to modernize and bringing the old games to today, especially because of this reason. A lot of QOL wouldn't even change the game/gameplay just remove frustration again with ZERO con. OVERALL THOUGH: I love this game, I highly recommend it even without ANYTHING I list in this "review" It's just because I love it so much I can see so much holding it back. While the community has nice people there are a lot of purists who hate any change regardless of what it is and this sucks and contributes to this game being further improved upon. - Compare inventory weapon/ring/etc. Unless I am blind as a bat I can't find this and comparing gear is a pain in the butt. Would love a compare tooltip whether it be by auto compare when hovering over weapons/geat/etc or manual key press/hold - Faster fishing, that's it. It's so boring compared to original fates (I dont care about the rng change, but this speed makes it entirely unfun) - Ability to remap **ALL** keybinds - Undo or buyback )For accidental sales) - Ability to spend gold to respec your character - A tool tip that shows what the symbol above mercenaries/companions do when you change them - Ability to scale hud down or up (For me the hud is way too big on 4k and my 45in monitor lol) - Better item/stat/etc descriptions (Somethings I have literally no idea what they do. Playing a hardcore character and hovering over revival charm or potion doesnt say whether it works only on you pet/companions or if you die. And if so if it works on hardcore characters or not). - Purchasable stash/inventory space increase whether by in game gold or real money (But if it is real money should be damn significant lol plus it helps support the devs) - More hotbar slots (Like in traitor soul/etc) - Loot filtering & Better rarity tooltip for drop items/gear. Select what quality of drops you want to see or hide. Make it easier to pick things up, it's pretty difficulty at times. - Mercenaries need work (They are constantly at times avoiding combat or just running around doing who knows what, getting stuck, etc) - The new dungeon dlc and any new dungeon dlc should be focused on Traitor Soul not Fate or Undiscovered Realms. Traitor soul is the combination + of those two, keep those two original. Traitor Soul makes the most sense for expanding on dungeons and hub world. OR at the least new dungeons and content added to undiscovered realms should also apply to traitor soul. - Shop refresh through paying gold (With gambler too). - Access to the games settings/options without having to leave the game. - An option to check for auto fishing. You click once, and it auto succeeds or fails. No click needed. [h1] Surprisingly Fun Despite Being a Hot Mess [/h1] [h3] Recommendation [/h3] If you're looking for a dungeon crawler game for kids, try Torchlight II before you get this game. Unlike Fate Reawakened, Torchlight II is easy to mod (and it doesn't need mods nearly as badly as Fate Reawakened does). If you do get Fate Reawakened game, get a hold of someone somewhat technical. You need both a mod tool as well as a mod that allows you to adjust the gold, experience, and fame you get in the game. I am not in any way joking when I say that you need 200 times the gold the game gives you. I found what I needed on Nexus Mods in case you want a place to start looking. [h3] The Hot Mess Part 1: The In-Game Economy [/h3] The in-game economy is something I could only see for truly die-hard gamers (and NOT for kids). The amount of gold you get versus what you need is utterly ridiculous. And the only thing I can figure is that the economy is so broken is because the developers didn't implement a tiered gear structure. What I mean by a tiered gear structure is what you will find in Torchlight II. You start out getting a piece of leather armor, and then you work on up to some kind of full plate mail. After that, it starts over. And now your piece of "epic" leather armor gives more protection than full plate mail. You will work up to "epic" full plate mail before you're back to a third tier of leather armor. Because the developers of Fate didn't want to mess around with the complicated spreadsheets necessary to make a tiered system of loot, you will trade out your gear very, very infrequently. Therefore, you get a lot less money. And as a result, the game is much less rewarding than just about every dungeon crawler I've ever played. And I've been playing dungeon crawlers since Diablo on Windows 95. And again, because of the above paragraphs about the game economy, the enchanter in the game is the harshest enchanter of any game I have ever played. It will screw up a piece of gear on a very regular basis. Why must that be the case? Because there is so very little gear in the game. Each masterpiece piece of gear that you get is what you will have until the very end of four chapters of the game. Therefore, each masterpiece is incredibly hard to get. [h3] The Hot Mess: Everything Else [/h3] You'll see an in-game tip tell you all about the jewelry that your pet can wear. That sounds great! And it would be, but you will have to remember to unequip and reequip your pet's jewelry every time you go down to a lower floor of the dungeon. Why do you need a button next to your quests so that you can cancel them? Because some quests cannot be completed. I found three bugs that cause quests to not register that you completed them. And I stopped accepting the "kill boss monster and his minions" quests because of how often I had to cancel them after I had fully completed the quest. Oh, look! You can import characters from the first Fate chapter to the next chapters in the game! How cool is that? Well, it would be cool, but the game has no idea what level you are when you import a character. So, you'll endure dozens of levels where you will literally run past enemies because they are not even worth your time. And the kicker about this is that the game can generate 2 billion labyrinth levels. Therefore, it would be DIRT SIMPLE for the developers to know exactly what level you are when you import a character. It's just incredibly poor execution. And in case you haven't read other reviews for this game, let me say that many other people have complained bitterly about the inability to remap key bindings. Therefore, if you have a controller, use it. The game's controller support is quite solid whereas the keyboard and mouse support is non-existent. [h3] Does this game do anything well? [/h3] The random generation of labyrinths is great, and some of the random battles in those labyrinths will be epic. There are also random treasure rooms full of loot while other floors will be desolate. The spells in Fate are better than spells in most dungeon crawlers. But you have to keep in mind that the game has no character classes. Therefore, once you make a wizard and a summoner, you're pretty much done making new characters. That's a good thing, too. Fate Reawaked was not made for replay value.
